mainTopic: Why the ערבה in the מקדש overrides שבת on the seventh day, and why it does not override שבת today
overview: This amud opens by finishing the source that a person must sit in the סוכה at night as well as by day, through a גזירה שוה from the word "תשבו" in the מילואים. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that the ערבה in the מקדש overrides שבת on the seventh day. רבי יוחנן explains that this publicizes that the ערבה is a Torah-level מצוה. A chain of challenges then explains why the לולב does not do the same, why the ערבה is not blocked by a decree, and why it overrides on the seventh day and not every day, the first day, or a middle day. Next the גמרא asks why the ערבה does not override שבת today. In בבל the reason is doubt about the calendar, and travelers from ארץ ישראל disagree about whether the seventh day even falls on שבת there. רב יוסף suggests the ערבה מצוה was only standing the branches by the מזבח, but אביי challenges him. A ברייתא about the בייתוסין then refutes רב יוסף and shows the ערבה was taken in hand. The amud ends with a new answer, that ארץ ישראל matches the practice of חוץ לארץ. That answer is challenged from the first day of סוכות, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Nights in the סוכה learned from the מילואים
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה from the word "תשבו" teaches that the מצוה of סוכה applies at night as well as by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You shall sit" and "you shall sit" make a word-link. It says "you shall sit" here, about סוכה, and "you shall sit" about the מילואים. There it means days and also nights, so here too it means days and also nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the source showing that one must live in the סוכה at night too, not only during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the same word "תשבו" for the סוכה and for the seven days of the מילואים. About the מילואים, the Torah says plainly "day and night." Because of the shared word, a גזירה שוה carries the "day and night" meaning over to סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A word-link: the same word in two places teaches that a law from one applies to the other
The seven-day inauguration of the משכן and the כהנים
"Just as there, so too here": the standard wording of a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: The obligation of סוכה covers all seven days and all seven nights, learned through the גזירה שוה "תשבו" "תשבו" from the מילואים.

phrases.english: "You shall sit," "you shall sit": for a verbal analogy.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא from the previous section.

phrases.english: It is said here "you shall sit,"
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in Leviticus 23:42, about סוכה.

phrases.english: and it is said about the inauguration "you shall sit."
phrases.notes: This is Leviticus 8:35, which says "day and night seven days."

phrases.english: Just as there, "days" means even nights,
so too here, "days" means even nights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source discussion on סוכה that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה of סוכה applies by night as well as by day, learned through the גזירה שוה "תשבו" from the מילואים.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the ערבה for seven days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the ערבה is taken seven days. How so?
steps.simpleTranslation: The ערבה is taken for seven days. How so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to begin a new topic. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the ערבה ritual is never done on שבת. The משנה explains that it reaches a full seven days only when the seventh day falls on שבת, because on that day it overrides שבת. That ruling is what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: The willow branch that was walked around the מזבח in the מקדש on סוכות
"How so?" The משנה's own word for introducing an explanation

phrases.english: The willow is seven days. How so?
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on to say that if the seventh day falls on שבת, the ערבה is still done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערבה is done for seven days only when its seventh day falls on שבת, since on that day it overrides שבת.

steps.title: Why does the seventh-day ערבה override שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the ערבה on the seventh day overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ערבה on the seventh day: what is the reason it overrides שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the seventh day of ערבה, out of all seven days, is strong enough to push aside שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the other six days, the ערבה does not override שבת. So the גמרא wants to know what is special about the seventh day.

phrases.english: The willow on the seventh day,
what is the reason it overrides Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲרָבָה בִּשְׁבִיעִי מַאי טַעְמָא דָּחֲיָא שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the ערבה on the seventh day overrides שבת.

steps.title: To publicize that the willow is a Torah מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that it overrides שבת to make known that the ערבה is a Torah-level מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is in order to publicize that it is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the reason: overriding שבת shows everyone that the ערבה is a real Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערבה in the מקדש is not written in the Torah. It is a הלכה למשה מסיני, so people might think it is only rabbinic. Doing it even on שבת shows that it carries Torah authority, since a rabbinic practice could never override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: To publicize it, to make it known
From the Torah, a Torah-level law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ערבה overrides שבת because it is more important than other מצוות. The point is to send a message about its status. It does this on only one day, so that people see it is Torah-level.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
in order to publicize that it is from the Torah.
phrases.notes: It is a הלכה למשה מסיני and is not written in the verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּדֵי לְפַרְסְמָהּ שֶׁהִיא מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ערבה overrides שבת to publicize that it is a Torah-level מצוה.

steps.title: Then the לולב should also override שבת
steps.stepSummary: If publicizing is a reason, the לולב should also override שבת on the other days, to show that it is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the לולב too should override שבת, in order to publicize that it is from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's reason: the same logic should apply to the לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש, the לולב is a Torah מצוה all seven days, but this is not clearly stated in the verses either. Yet the לולב overrides שבת only on the first day. If publicizing were enough of a reason, the לולב should override שבת on the other days too.

keyTerms.meaning: "If so": introduces a challenge based on the previous answer
The palm branch taken on סוכות

phrases.english: If so, the lulav too should override [Shabbat],
in order to publicize that it is from the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reason that publicizing Torah status justifies overriding שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reason applies to the לולב, yet the לולב does not override שבת on the later days.

steps.title: The לולב is restricted by רבה's decree
steps.stepSummary: The לולב is held back by רבה's decree: a person might carry it in the public domain to learn how to use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לולב is restricted by a decree, because of רבה's concern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the לולב has a special problem: the Rabbis decreed against it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה worried that a person might carry the לולב in the street on שבת, bringing it to an expert to learn how to shake it. That concern blocks the לולב on שבת, even though the publicizing reason would otherwise apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

phrases.english: The lulav: a decree due to Rabbah's concern.
phrases.notes: The concern is that one might carry the לולב four אמות in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: the לולב has a separate blocking decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לולב should override שבת like the ערבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה's decree against carrying prevents the לולב from overriding שבת.

steps.title: Then decree on the willow as well
steps.stepSummary: If the לולב is restricted by רבה's decree, the same decree should apply to the ערבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us make the same decree for the ערבה too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the carrying concern should apply equally to the ערבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערבה is also an object that could be carried on שבת. So why should רבה's decree block the לולב but not the ערבה?

phrases.english: If so, let us decree on the willow as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of רבה's decree to separate the לולב from the ערבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The carrying concern seems to apply equally to the ערבה.

steps.title: Court agents bring the ערבה; the לולב is up to everyone
steps.stepSummary: Agents of the court bring the ערבה, so there is no risk. Each individual handles his own לולב, so there is a risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ערבה: agents of the court bring it. The לולב: it is handed over to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the decree applies only to the לולב: who handles the object makes all the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערבה is prepared before שבת by שלוחי בית דין, careful agents of the court, so no one will carry it wrongly. The לולב is taken by every ordinary person, some of whom might carry it in public. So the danger exists only with the לולב.

keyTerms.meaning: "Handed over to everyone," every individual's responsibility

phrases.aramaic: עֲרָבָה — שְׁלוּחֵי בֵּית דִּין מַיְיתִי לַהּ.
phrases.english: The willow: agents of the court bring it.
The lulav: it is given over to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲרָבָה — שְׁלוּחֵי בֵּית דִּין מַיְיתִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction: who handles the object.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The carrying decree should cover the ערבה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ערבה is handled by careful court agents, so there is no carrying risk. The decree applies only to the לולב.

steps.title: Then the ערבה should override שבת every day
steps.stepSummary: If the ערבה carries no carrying risk, it should override שבת on all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should override שבת every day too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again: if the ערבה is safe from the decree, why limit it to the seventh day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערבה has two things going for it: the reason to publicize, and no carrying risk. So nothing seems to stop it from overriding שבת on any day of סוכות.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, כׇּל יוֹמָא נָמֵי לִידְחֵי!
phrases.english: If so, it should override [Shabbat] every day too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כׇּל יוֹמָא נָמֵי לִידְחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new challenge out of the answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the ערבה's overriding of שבת to the seventh day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing seems to prevent the ערבה from overriding שבת on all seven days.

steps.title: People would doubt the importance of the לולב
steps.stepSummary: If the ערבה overrode שבת all week while the לולב overrides only one day, people would come to look down on the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: People would come to have doubts about the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that letting the ערבה override שבת every day would make the לולב look less important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לולב, which is written in the Torah, overrides שבת on only one day. If the ערבה overrode it every day, people would conclude the לולב is less serious. To avoid that, the ערבה is limited to one day.

keyTerms.meaning: To raise doubts about, to belittle

phrases.english: They would come to raise doubts about the lulav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Policy concern about how people would perceive the מצוות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ערבה should override שבת every day.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is limited to one day so the לולב is not belittled.

steps.title: Then let the willow override on the first day
steps.stepSummary: If the ערבה gets only one day, why not the first day, like the לולב?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it override on the first day of יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the one day chosen for the ערבה is the seventh day and not the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first day is when the לולב overrides שבת. It might seem natural to let the ערבה override on that same day.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the festival

phrases.english: And let it override on the first day of the Festival!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question after step 10 limited the ערבה to one day.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the seventh day rather than the first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only one day is allowed, the first day seems the natural choice, matching the לולב.

steps.title: On the first day the message would be lost
steps.stepSummary: On the first day, people would think it is the לולב that overrides שבת, and that the ערבה just comes along with it. So the publicity would fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter would not be clear. People would say: it is the לולב that is overriding שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that on the first day, the point of publicizing would be lost, because people would credit the לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole reason for the ערבה overriding שבת is to show that it is a Torah law. On the first day, people would assume the ערבה is allowed only because of the לולב. Only on the seventh day, when the לולב does not override שבת, does the ערבה clearly stand on its own.
steps.whatToRemember: The ערבה overrides שבת only on the seventh day for four reasons. It publicizes that it is Torah law. It has no carrying risk, since court agents handle it. It is not every day, so the לולב is not belittled. And it is not the first day, because there the message would be credited to the לולב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the precise wording of the משנה. It also shows how a publicity-based law must be shaped so that its message is actually seen.

phrases.english: The matter would not be evident;
they would say: it is the lulav that is overriding [Shabbat].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11. Step 13 then asks why the seventh day and not one of the middle days.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the goal of publicizing would be defeated on the first day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ערבה could override שבת on the first day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only on the seventh day is it clear that the ערבה itself overrides שבת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ערבה overrides שבת specifically on the seventh day, because only there is its Torah status publicly visible.

steps.title: Why not one of the middle days?
steps.stepSummary: If the ערבה cannot override שבת on the first day, let it override שבת on one of the middle days instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it override שבת on one of these other days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: we moved the ערבה away from the first day, but why did it land on the seventh day and not one of the middle days of סוכות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 explained why the first day does not work for publicizing the ערבה. That leaves days two through seven as options. The question is why the seventh day was singled out.

phrases.english: And let it override on one of these other days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 12 and asks for the next choice of day
steps.kashyaTarget: Choosing the seventh day for the ערבה to override שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the first day is ruled out, any of the remaining days should work equally well. So why specifically the seventh?

steps.title: Moved from the first, placed on the seventh
steps.stepSummary: Once the ערבה is moved off the first day, it is placed on the seventh day, the other special day of the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since you are moving it off the first day, set it on the seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the seventh day is the natural second choice after the first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first and the last days of the חג are the two days that stand out. Once the first day is ruled out, the ערבה goes to the other standout day, the seventh, and not to an ordinary middle day.

keyTerms.meaning: You are taking it out / moving it

phrases.english: Since you are moving it from the first day,
establish it on the seventh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical preference for the other distinguished day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any of the remaining days would be just as good
steps.terutzMaskana: The seventh day, the final special day, is the natural replacement for the first
steps.whatToRemember: The ערבה overrides שבת only on the seventh day because the first day would confuse people with the לולב, and the seventh is the other special day.

steps.title: Then why not override שבת nowadays?
steps.stepSummary: If the ערבה is important enough to override שבת, it should override שבת today as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should override שבת today too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question: if the seventh-day ערבה overrides שבת, why don't we do that today?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything so far explained the rule as it worked when the בית המקדש stood. The challenge asks why the rule should not carry over to the present day.

phrases.english: If so, nowadays too let it override!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the established rule and tests whether it applies today
steps.kashyaTarget: Current practice of not taking the ערבה on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason was publicity and there was no carrying risk, the same reasoning should still apply today.

steps.title: We don't know the exact calendar
steps.stepSummary: In בבל we are unsure of the exact date set by בית דין, so we cannot know which day is really the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not know the fixing of the month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we in בבל are not sure which day is truly the seventh, so we cannot override שבת for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new month was set by בית דין in ארץ ישראל, and people far away were not sure of the date. If we are not sure that today is really the seventh day, we cannot override שבת for a מצוה that may not apply today.

keyTerms.meaning: The fixing of the month (by בית דין)

phrases.english: We do not know
the fixing of the month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual uncertainty prevents the rule from applying
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ערבה should override שבת today just as before
steps.terutzMaskana: Doubt about the true date stops us from overriding שבת

steps.title: Those who know the calendar should do it
steps.stepSummary: The people of ארץ ישראל do know the calendar, so they should override שבת for the ערבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They, who do know the fixing of the month, should override!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the uncertainty answer only works for us in בבל, so in ארץ ישראל they should still override שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16's answer depends on not knowing the date. People in ארץ ישראל lived near the בית דין and knew the date for sure, so the answer does not cover them.

phrases.english: They, who know the fixing of the month —
let them override!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 16 to בבל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer does not apply to people who know the date for sure, so they should still override שבת.

steps.title: בר הדיא: It never falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: בר הדיא reported from ארץ ישראל that the seventh day of סוכות never falls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When בר הדיא came, he said: it does not happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report from בר הדיא that the question never comes up in ארץ ישראל, because the seventh day never lands on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The calendar was arranged so that הושענא רבה would not fall on שבת. So the people of ארץ ישראל never face the question, and nothing contradicts the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: בר הדיא, a traveler who brought reports from ארץ ישראל
It does not happen / does not coincide

phrases.english: When Bar Hedya came, he said:
It does not coincide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 with a factual report
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The people of ארץ ישראל, who know the date, should override שבת for the ערבה
steps.terutzMaskana: The seventh day never falls on שבת there, so there is no question

steps.title: רבין: It does happen, but they don't override
steps.stepSummary: רבין and the other travelers reported that the seventh day does fall on שבת, but the ערבה does not override it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין and all the travelers came, they said: it does happen, and it does not override.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report from ארץ ישראל disagrees with בר הדיא: the seventh day does fall on שבת, and they still do not take the ערבה. This brings the question back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבין is right, בר הדיא's answer no longer works. Now there is a real case in ארץ ישראל where people know the date and still do not override שבת, so an explanation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: רבין, an אמורא who brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל
Those who 'went down,' the travelers between ארץ ישראל and בבל

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין וְכׇל נָחוֹתֵי, אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: When Ravin and all the travelers came, they said:
It does coincide, and it does not override.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין וְכׇל נָחוֹתֵי, אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with בר הדיא's report and brings the question of step 17 back
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל the seventh day sometimes falls on שבת, and the ערבה does not override it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבין is not answering the question; he is reporting a fact that makes the question harder. That is why the גמרא next says 'it is still difficult.'

steps.title: Then the question returns
steps.stepSummary: According to רבין's report, the difficulty is back: why don't they override שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then it is difficult?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states openly that, according to רבין, the question from step 17 has no answer yet. This line sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of ארץ ישראל know the date and the day does fall on שבת, yet they do not take the ערבה. That seems to go against the rule of the משנה.

phrases.english: But then it is difficult?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the problem out of רבין's report
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calendar doubt does not apply, and the day does fall on שבת, so they should override שבת.

steps.title: Maybe the ערבה מצוה is standing it by the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף: perhaps the ערבה מצוה is not taking it in the hand but standing it up beside the מזבח, which is impossible today.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Who says the ערבה מצוה is done by taking it? Perhaps it is done by standing it up!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that the ערבה that overrides שבת may have been the branches set up around the מזבח, and with no מזבח today there is nothing to override שבת for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to understand the ערבה מצוה: holding it (נטילה), or standing it up by the מזבח (זקיפה). If it is זקיפה, it needs a מזבח. Without the בית המקדש, the מצוה that overrode שבת cannot be done, so ארץ ישראל does not override שבת either.

keyTerms.meaning: Who will tell us? / Who says?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Who will tell us that the willow is by taking?
Perhaps it is by standing upright!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאן לֵימָא לַן דַּעֲרָבָה בִּנְטִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining how the מצוה is done
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ערבה מצוה is holding it, which can still be done today
steps.terutzMaskana: It may be standing it by the מזבח, which needs the בית המקדש, so it does not override שבת today
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף suggests that the ערבה מצוה may be standing the branches beside the מזבח (זקיפה), which needs a מזבח. That would explain why ארץ ישראל does not override שבת today. אביי challenges this suggestion in the steps that follow, and it is refuted in step 33.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the ערבה מצוה were only זקיפה beside the מזבח, that would explain why ארץ ישראל does not override שבת today even though they know the date. The rest of the amud tests this idea, and in the end the גמרא rejects it.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה pairs לולב and ערבה, so both are taken in hand
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites the משנה 'לולב וערבה ששה ושבעה' and argues that the ערבה is compared to the לולב. Just as the לולב is held in the hand, so is the ערבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: The משנה says 'לולב and ערבה, six and seven days.' Doesn't this mean the ערבה is like the לולב? Just as the לולב מצוה is done by taking it in hand, so too the ערבה מצוה is done by taking it in hand!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's idea that the ערבה מצוה is only standing it beside the מזבח. He uses a משנה that mentions לולב and ערבה side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the two מצוות together in one phrase. אביי reads this as a comparison: the ערבה should be done the same way as the לולב, by holding it. If so, רב יוסף's suggestion of standing it up falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (usually from a משנה or ברייתא)
Taking or holding in the hand
Is it not? (introduces a suggested reading of a source)
Six or seven (days), depending on which weekday the festival starts

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
Lulav and willow: six or seven days.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה from earlier in the פרק.

phrases.english: Is it not that it is like lulav:
just as lulav is done by taking it,
so too willow is done by taking it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's suggestion in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's suggestion that the ערבה מצוה is standing it beside the מזבח, not holding it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה pairs ערבה with לולב, which implies the same method of performance: taking in hand.

steps.title: Each מצוה keeps its own method
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that listing the two together proves nothing about how each is done. The לולב is held and the ערבה is stood up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real comparison? This one is done its way, and that one is done its way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects אביי's comparison. Being listed together in the משנה does not mean the two מצוות are performed the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only links them in how many days they last, six or seven. It says nothing about the method. So the לולב can be held while the ערבה is stood beside the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is, in its own way

phrases.english: Are these comparable?
This one is as it is,
and that one is as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the analogy: the shared listing concerns only the number of days, not the method.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה lists לולב and ערבה together, they must be performed the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each מצוה has its own method. The לולב is held, and the ערבה may be stood beside the מזבח.

steps.title: אביי: they circled the altar with the willow
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites the משנה that the people circled the מזבח once each day and seven times on the seventh day. He suggests they did this holding the ערבה, which would mean the ערבה was held in the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: Every day they circle the מזבח once, and on that day, the seventh, seven times. Isn't that with the ערבה in hand?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries a second proof that the ערבה was held. He points to the people walking around the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people walked around the מזבח holding ערבות, then the ערבה מצוה involved holding it. That would contradict רב יוסף, who said it was only stood up.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ פַּעַם אַחַת,
phrases.english: Every day they circle the altar one time,
and on that day, seven times.
Is it not with the willow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב יוסף, after the first was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the ערבה is stood up, not held
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The circling was done with the ערבה in hand, so the ערבה was held.

steps.title: No, they circled with the לולב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the people circled holding the לולב, not the ערבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it was with the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says the משנה about circling refers to holding the לולב. That leaves no proof about the ערבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never says what the people held while circling. By saying it was the לולב, רב יוסף removes אביי's proof and keeps his idea that the ערבה was only stood up.

phrases.english: No, with the lulav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the source: the circling was done with the לולב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They circled the מזבח holding the ערבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They circled holding the לולב, so nothing is proven about the ערבה.

steps.title: But רב נחמן said it was with the willow
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, said the circling was done with the ערבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: it was with the ערבה!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's answer by citing another אמורא who said the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's answer depends on the circling being done with the לולב. אביי shows that an earlier authority explicitly said it was the ערבה, which would bring the challenge back.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (cites a statement against the answer)
An אמורא whose teaching רב נחמן often reports

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Nachman say
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
with the willow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading that the circling was with the לולב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An established אמורא tradition says the circling was with the ערבה.

steps.title: He says ערבה, I say לולב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that רבה בר אבוה is entitled to his view, and he himself holds it was the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He told you it was the ערבה, and I say it was the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף does not try to explain away רבה בר אבוה. He simply disagrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's statement does not bind another אמורא. Since both are אמוראים, רב יוסף is allowed to hold the other view, that the circling was with the לולב.

keyTerms.meaning: And I say (introduces a disagreeing opinion)

phrases.english: He said to him:
He told you with the willow,
and I say with the lulav.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אָמַר לָךְ בַּעֲרָבָה, וַאֲנָא אָמֵינָא בְּלוּלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement among אמוראים: רב יוסף holds the other opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה בר אבוה's statement settles that the circling was with the ערבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: This is a dispute, and רב יוסף holds it was the לולב.

steps.title: The אמוראים disagree: לולב or ערבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא records a dispute. רבי אלעזר says the circling was with the לולב. רבי חנינא, quoted by רב שמואל בר נתן, says it was with the ערבה, and so did רבה בר אבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי אלעזר says it was with the לולב. רב שמואל בר נתן said in the name of רבי חנינא: with the ערבה. And likewise רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: with the ערבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms that רב יוסף's answer matches a real, earlier dispute among the אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף is not alone. רבי אלעזר also held the circling was with the לולב. The view that it was with the ערבה belongs to רבי חנינא and רבה בר אבוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a recorded dispute among אמוראים)

phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Elazar says: with the lulav.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל [בַּר נָתָן] אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: בַּעֲרָבָה.
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Natan said that Rabbi Chanina said: with the willow.
And likewise Rav Nachman said
that Rabba bar Avuh said: with the willow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 27 by showing the dispute already existed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute among אמוראים. רבי אלעזר says the circling was with the לולב. רבי חנינא and רבה בר אבוה say it was with the ערבה.

steps.title: רבא reports רבי אלעזר's view through רבה בר בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב יצחק, the son of רבה בר בר חנה, that his father taught in the name of רבי אלעזר that the circling in the משנה was done with the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב יצחק, son of רבה בר בר חנה: Son of Torah, come and I will tell you an excellent teaching your father used to say. About the משנה, 'Every day they circle the מזבח once, and on that day they circle the מזבח seven times,' your father said in the name of רבי אלעזר: with the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another tradition, passed through רבה בר בר חנה, that backs רבי אלעזר's view: the circling was with the לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that רבי אלעזר really held this view, because it reached רבא through a second chain of tradition. It adds weight to רב יוסף's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of Torah, a term of affection for a learned person
That which we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Rava said to

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak, son of Rabba bar bar Chana:
Son of Torah, come and I will tell you
an excellent teaching that your father used to say.
That which we learned in a mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַיּוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ פַּעַם אַחַת,
phrases.english: Every day they circle the altar one time,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים,
phrases.english: and on that day they circle the altar seven times,
this is what your father said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar: with the lulav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second line of tradition for רבי אלעזר's view from step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, as passed down by רבה בר בר חנה, the circling of the מזבח was done with the לולב.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a dispute about what the people held while circling the מזבח. רבי אלעזר and רב יוסף say the לולב. רבי חנינא and רבה בר אבוה say the ערבה.

steps.title: אביי opens a challenge from the story of the בייתוסין
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: the לולב overrides שבת at the start of the festival and the ערבה at the end. Once the seventh day fell on שבת, and the ערבה branches were brought before שבת and placed in the עזרה. The בייתוסין took them and hid them under stones. The story continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: The לולב overrides שבת at the beginning of the festival, and the ערבה at the end. Once the seventh day of ערבה fell on שבת. They brought large ערבה branches on ערב שבת and placed them in the עזרה. The בייתוסין recognized them, took them, and pressed them under stones.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins a third challenge to רב יוסף using a ברייתא and a story from the בית המקדש. The גמרא is setting up the challenge here, and its full point will come as the story continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first says the ערבה overrides שבת on the seventh day. Then it tells how the בייתוסין, who rejected this practice, hid the branches so the מצוה could not be done on שבת. The continuation will show how the ערבה was actually used that day, and that detail will become the basis of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the בית המקדש
Boethusians, a sect that rejected the oral tradition
They pressed them down, hid them

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not finished. The ברייתא's story continues next, and the actual force of אביי's challenge depends on that continuation.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
Lulav overrides Shabbat at its beginning,
and willow at its end.

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת חָל שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל עֲרָבָה
phrases.english: Once the seventh day of willow occurred
on Shabbat,
and they brought large branches of willow
on Shabbat eve
and placed them in the Temple courtyard.
The Boethusians recognized them,
and took them and pressed them under stones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: לוּלָב דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת בִּתְחִלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to רב יוסף's suggestion in step 21, after the circling discussion ended in a dispute
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's suggestion about how the ערבה מצוה is performed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: a ברייתא describing how the ערבה was handled when the seventh day fell on שבת. The decisive detail comes in the story's continuation.

steps.title: End of the story: the branches are rescued and stood by the altar
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes. The next day the עמי הארץ found the ערבה branches, pulled them out, and the כהנים stood them up at the sides of the מזבח. All this happened because the בייתוסין deny that beating the ערבה overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day the עמי הארץ noticed the branches and pulled them out from under the stones. The כהנים brought them and stood them upright at the sides of the מזבח. This happened because the בייתוסין do not agree that beating the ערבה overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the ברייתא that אביי quoted against רב יוסף. It tells us how the hidden ערבה branches got back to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains why the בייתוסין hid the branches: they rejected the idea that beating the ערבה (חיבוט) overrides שבת. The phrase 'beating the ערבה' is the key detail. It shows that the ערבה מצוה involved handling the branches, not only standing them up.

keyTerms.meaning: Unlearned common people. Here they were loyal to the חכמים, even though they did not know all the details.
Boethusians, a sect that rejected the חכמים' oral tradition.
Beating or waving the willow branch.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at 'they stood them by the מזבח' and conclude that standing them up was the whole מצוה. The last line of the ברייתא speaks of beating (חיבוט) the ערבה, and that detail is what drives the proof in the next step.

phrases.english: The next day the ignorant common people noticed them,
and pulled them out from under the stones,
and the priests brought them
and stood them upright at the sides of the altar.
Because the Boethusians do not agree
that beating the willow overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that the ערבה in the מקדש was not taken in hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes beating the ערבה on שבת, so the ערבה was handled, not merely stood up.

steps.title: The inference: the willow מצוה is done by taking it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that the ערבה מצוה is done through נטילה, taking it in hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that it is done by taking it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the story. The ערבה was taken in hand, so the מצוה involves נטילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מצוה were only standing the branches by the מזבח, the ברייתא would not speak of beating them, and there would be nothing for the בייתוסין to fight over. Because the ברייתא speaks of beating the ערבה, the מצוה must involve taking it, which contradicts רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently / so we see (introduces a conclusion drawn from a source).

phrases.english: So we see it is done by taking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in steps 30-31.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows נטילה, which contradicts רב יוסף's view.

steps.title: רב יוסף is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that רב יוסף's view is conclusively refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: A refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that רב יוסף's position cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא is the strongest kind of rejection: the view is overturned, not just questioned. From now on we hold that the ערבה מצוה is done by taking it in hand.
steps.whatToRemember: The ערבה מצוה in the מקדש was done by taking it in hand (נטילה). רב יוסף's view is rejected.
steps.whyThisMatters: Now that the ערבה is known to be taken in hand, the old question of why it does not override שבת today comes back.

phrases.english: A refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seals the inference of step 32.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף is refuted. The ערבה is taken in hand (נטילה).

steps.title: So why not override שבת for the ערבה today?
steps.stepSummary: With רב יוסף refuted, the original question returns: let people take the ערבה on שבת today.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, let them override שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier question. Since רב יוסף's explanation fell, why don't they take the ערבה on שבת nowadays?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had explained why the ערבה does not override שבת today, and that explanation is gone. In ארץ ישראל they know the correct day, so the גמרא asks why they do not override שבת for the ערבה.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather / if so (reopens a question).

phrases.english: But then, let them override!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reopens the original question now that רב יוסף's answer is refuted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The current practice of not taking the ערבה on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ערבה is a נטילה מצוה that overrides שבת, ארץ ישראל should still do it on שבת.

steps.title: Since we in the Diaspora don't, they don't either
steps.stepSummary: ארץ ישראל does not override שבת for the ערבה because חוץ לארץ does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we do not override, they also do not override.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ארץ ישראל follows the same practice as חוץ לארץ, so neither one overrides שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חוץ לארץ they cannot override שבת, because they are unsure of the exact date. The answer suggests that ארץ ישראל keeps a matching practice so the two communities stay uniform.

keyTerms.meaning: We (here, the people of חוץ לארץ).
They (here, the people of ארץ ישראל).

phrases.english: Since we do not override,
they also do not override.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uniform practice between ארץ ישראל and חוץ לארץ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ארץ ישראל should override שבת, since they know the date.
steps.terutzMaskana: They hold back so their practice matches חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: But on the first day of סוכות, practice differs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that answer: on the first day of סוכות, ארץ ישראל takes the לולב on שבת even though חוץ לארץ does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the first day of the festival? For us it does not override שבת, and for them it does!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 35 with a counterexample from the לולב on the first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the לולב on the first day, the two places act differently, so a 'we must match' rule does not exist. That undermines the answer, and the גמרא takes up the question again on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the festival.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ארץ ישראל matches חוץ לארץ practice.
